extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners working on headline generation, controllable text generation, and computational journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Rewriting news headlines with LLMs to increase reader engagement (clickability) while avoiding clickbait, using controllable generation and guidance models to balance attractiveness and semantic fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader engagement / clickability
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhancing reader engagement while preserving informational fidelity is a central challenge in controllable text generation for news media; optimizing news headlines for reader engagement is often conflated with clickbait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system should increase clickability/attractiveness of headlines while distinguishing such optimization from clickbait; engagement is an explicit objective guided by an engagement-attribute model and balanced against faithfulness and proportional emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informational fidelity / semantic preservation / semantic faithfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve informational fidelity of the original headline/article; enforce explicit constraints on semantic faithfulness during rewriting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines must maintain the original information content; semantic preservation is an explicit constraint in the controllable generation formulation and a primary axis in the trade-off with attractiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clickbait avoidance (conceptualized as suppression of disproportionate amplification)
rubrics_metrics.description: View clickbait not as a separate stylistic category but as an extreme outcome of disproportionate amplification of otherwise legitimate engagement cues; avoid such excessive amplification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use negative guidance (a clickbait scoring model) to suppress excessive stylistic amplification; measure and penalize disproportionate emphasis that would produce clickbait-like exaggeration or misleading phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional emphasis (avoid disproportionate amplification of engagement cues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure emphasis on engagement cues is proportional and not exaggerated relative to the factual content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewriting must enforce constraints on proportional emphasis so that legitimate engagement tactics are not amplified to the point of misrepresentation; this is modeled explicitly as a constraint during controllable generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective strengthening of engagement-oriented linguistic attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific engagement-oriented linguistic attributes may be selectively strengthened to meet target clickability objectives under constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An engagement-attribute guide provides positive guidance to amplify chosen linguistic attributes; the selection and degree of strengthening should be controllable and aligned with editorial targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clickbait scoring model as negative guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A clickbait scoring model provides negative guidance to suppress excessive stylistic amplification that leads to clickbait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clickbait scorer is used at inference time to steer the LLM away from headlines that have high clickbait scores; it should be trained on neutral headlines and used to impose penalties or lower probability for excessive amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement-attribute model as positive guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: An engagement-attribute model provides positive guidance aligned with target clickability objectives to encourage desirable engagement cues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guide boosts the probability of linguistic attributes associated with engagement; its outputs should be aligned with editorially acceptable engagement tactics and tuned together with negative guidance to balance outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inference-time controllability via FUDGE and adjustable guidance weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the FUDGE paradigm for inference-time control and adjust guidance weights to generate headlines along a continuum from neutral paraphrases to more engaging formulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust guidance weights at inference time to navigate the trade-off between attractiveness and faithfulness; the method should allow continuous, fine-grained control rather than discrete categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training data constraint: guides trained on neutral headlines from a curated real-world news corpus
rubrics_metrics.description: Both guide models are trained on neutral headlines drawn from a curated real-world news corpus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides should be learned from neutral (non-clickbait) headlines to define baselines for acceptable phrasing; dataset curation affects the behavior and calibration of both positive and negative guidance models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthetic generation of clickbait variants via controlled activation of predefined engagement tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Clickbait variants are generated synthetically by rewriting original headlines using an LLM under controlled activation of predefined engagement tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use synthetic LLM rewrites with controlled tactic activation to produce training examples of amplified headlines; this supports learning the boundary between acceptable engagement and clickbait for the guides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial acceptability and responsible LLM-based headline optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes should be editorially acceptable and support responsible headline optimization in journalistic settings, balancing attractiveness, semantic preservation, and clickbait avoidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must prioritize editorial trust and responsibility: aim for formulations that increase engagement without undermining informational fidelity or editorial standards; treat the trade-offs explicitly and provide control to editors.
